s01.text: FlashAttention is famous for being fast. That is the least interesting thing about it.

s02.text: The interesting thing is that it is not a faster kernel. It is a different order of operations.

s03.text: Attention has three steps. Multiply the queries and keys. Softmax the scores. Multiply by the values.

s04.text: The slow part is the middle one. The score matrix is sequence length by sequence length.

s05.text: At eight thousand tokens that is sixty-seven million numbers per head, written out to memory.

s06.text: And then read straight back. That round trip is what costs the time.

s07.text: FlashAttention never writes the score matrix down. It tiles it.

s08.text: It computes a block of scores in fast memory, softmaxes that block, multiplies it into the output, and throws it away.

s09.text: So the huge matrix never exists anywhere. Not on disk, not in video memory.

s10.text: The memory traffic drops from quadratic to linear, and the flops stay exactly the same.

s11.text: Same mathematics. Same answer. A completely different memory access pattern.

s12.text: Which is why the name is a bit of a joke. It is not about attention. It is about not writing things down.

s13.text: The fastest kernels are the ones that touch memory least.
